I had a big meeting scheduled that afternoon, the kind where I actually wanted to make a decent impression.
I decided lunch beforehand should be a healthy spinach salad from the place downstairs.
I ate at my desk, scrolling through emails, feeling pretty good about my responsible lunch choice.
I had no idea a tiny piece of spinach had settled itself right between my two front teeth.
I even remember thinking, at some point between bites, that I should eat salads more often.
I felt genuinely proud of myself for making such a mature, adult decision about my own lunch.
I walked into the meeting a little early.
I smiled at a few coworkers, made some small talk with someone from another department, and sat down feeling fairly confident about how the whole thing would go.
The meeting went fine, honestly, better than fine.
People nodded along to my points, and I even got a small compliment on an idea I'd pitched.
That only made me smile more throughout the entire thing.
At one point I even leaned forward, smiling confidently and making eye contact with basically everyone in the room.
I felt like I was really nailing the whole professional, put-together thing that day.
It wasn't until I got back to my desk that I saw it.
I'd opened my laptop's camera for an unrelated reason, and there it was, a very obvious, very green piece of spinach, smiling right back at me.
I mentally replayed the entire meeting in horror.
Every smile, every point I'd made while nodding enthusiastically, all done with a piece of spinach just sitting there the whole time, completely unbothered.
A coworker walked by, and I asked her, a little desperately, why nobody had said anything.
She just shrugged and said she genuinely hadn't noticed.
Honestly, that didn't make me feel much better, especially since she'd literally sat across from me the entire meeting.
I spent the rest of the afternoon a little paranoid, checking my teeth in every reflective surface I passed, a laptop screen, a dark window, even the back of my phone.
I even texted my sister the whole story, mostly just to have someone else suffer through the secondhand embarrassment with me.
She immediately sent back three separate messages, all just laughing emojis, no actual words at all.
Now I keep a tiny mirror in my desk drawer, and I check it religiously after literally anything green.
I promised myself I would never again walk into an important meeting smiling like a very confident salad.
My coworker still brings it up occasionally too, usually right as I'm about to eat lunch.
